findings.reason: the followup body is the dispatch order the plan carries, and adding the §7 step (and noting §2's held merge) is a one-line edit that changes what the coordinator runs next.
findings.text: the plan declares §2's merge gated on §7 (gate g-tstb-browser-row, line 133 + line 169) yet its own dispatch followup f-tstb-002 lists only "§2 and §3 in parallel; §4 then §5", omitting the implementable §7 that unblocks §2, so a coordinator working the followup sequence would dispatch §2, §3, §4 and §5 and never §7, leaving §2's merge held by its own gate indefinitely

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §7's cited files (tests/conftest.py, tests/spa_browser_harness.py, reckon/crew/standing_suite.py, docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml), gate g-tstb-browser-row, comment c-hold-s2-1010 and the extension-bearing /reckon/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head.html link all resolve; in the unchanged context §3's line anchors have drifted (line 83 cites _result_counts at 164 but it is now at 171), which does not change the plan.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §7's done-when (line 133) measures a universal over the marked population ("every collected test in every module importing the harness carries the marker") plus a negative ("no test outside those modules does"), and names a declared negative control (removing the marker exclusion collects a marked test and the assertion fails); a hook that marked nothing would fail its own positive assertion.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7's quiet-node measurement is written to the run directory and its failing ids to the-suite-is-green-at-head, both durable surfaces the host allocation names, not a session scratchpad or node-local /tmp; the fixed pytest log is a test fixture, not the gate evidence.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §7 carries no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into code or comments; the gate and comment identifiers (g-tstb-browser-row, c-hold-s2-1010) stay in plan data where they belong.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §7's root cause (the population's wall-clock, with timeouts confounded by a head arm run at a lower per-test timeout than the base) matches comment c-hold-s2-1010; the collection-time marker plus command exclusion mechanism is capable of producing the done-when; and each mechanism's caller is named and real (pytest_collection_modifyitems in tests/conftest.py, review.suite.command in docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml, reckon/crew/standing_suite.py).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 carries one deliverable: the browser population runs as its own suite row (marker, command exclusion, own record row, quiet-node measurement are facets of that one goal; line 133), and §6 is the only no-done-when section and is explicitly deferred.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §7's gate g-tstb-browser-row is declared (docs/plans/the-suite-tests-behaviour.html:169, data-gated-sections="s2", required evidence §7) and §7 states §2's completion is gated on its evidence, but the driving followup f-tstb-002 (line 145) sequences "§2 and §3 in parallel; §4 then §5" and never names §7, so the gate that holds §2's merge is not carried into the plan's own dispatch guidance.
